data.expected_signal: max abs error of kernel output vs exact erf over all finite FP16 values, and whether it exceeds 1e-6

evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 values: kernel max abs error vs exact (FP64) erf is 1.2918e-6 at x≈0.5083, with 1,394 values exceeding the 1e-6 absolute tolerance; 1,388 of those fall in the predicted 0.3<|x|<3 mid-range. The truncated-coefficient formula evaluated alone in FP64 already violates on 1,060 values (max 1.0627e-6 at x≈0.4968), confirming coefficient truncation is the decisive cause. Tolerance is absolute-only per contract, so this is a confirmed in-scope violation.

rationale: The kernel uses truncated constants 1.06141, -1.45315, 1.42141, -0.28450, 0.25483 instead of the full A&S values; per-coefficient truncation errors up to ~4.6e-6 weighted by the Gaussian envelope can produce total error above 1e-6 in the region 0.3<|x|<3 where exp(-x^2) is still near 1, violating the fixed absolute tolerance.

scope_evidence.summary: "Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - erf(x[i])) <= 1e-6. The relative tolerance is zero" and "EVERY finite FP16 value is legal" and "it is not defined by any specific polynomial ... if they meet this fixed absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain."

scope_rationale: The contract requires abs error <= 1e-6 for every element over every finite FP16 value; the truncated-coefficient A&S evaluation may exceed this in the mid-range, which is squarely inside the stated legal domain.
statement: The truncated A&S coefficients (1.06141, -1.45315, 1.42141, -0.28450, 0.25483) cause the kernel output to exceed the 1e-6 absolute tolerance against exact erf for some finite FP16 inputs in roughly 0.3<|x|<3, where the Gaussian envelope is still near 1.

data.expected_signal: isolate FP32 evaluation-chain error: kernel output minus the identical truncated-coefficient formula evaluated in FP64, over all finite FP16 values

evidence.summary: Isolating the FP32 evaluation chain by comparing kernel output to the identical truncated-coefficient formula evaluated in FP64 over all 63,488 finite FP16 values: the evaluation-chain error never exceeds 1e-6 (max 6.068e-7, only 52 values above 5e-7). The truncated formula alone already violates the tolerance (1,060 values, max 1.0627e-6), so coefficient truncation — not the FP32 evaluation chain (div_rn/tl.exp/Horner with fusion off) — is what pushes the total above the 1e-6 bar.

rationale: tl.exp compiles to fast GPU exp whose accuracy is ~1 ulp relative but can be worse; combined with Horner-chain rounding in FP32 this could push borderline cases over the 1e-6 bar even where coefficient error alone stays just under it.

scope_evidence.summary: "Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - erf(x[i])) <= 1e-6" with relative tolerance zero, for every finite FP16 value in the frozen T4/Triton 3.4 environment.

scope_rationale: The tolerance contract applies on the frozen T4/Triton 3.4 hardware, so the actual tl.exp accuracy there is part of the budget; error contributions add on top of coefficient truncation.
statement: The FP32 evaluation chain in the Triton kernel (tl.div_rn, tl.exp for exp(-x^2), FP32 Horner evaluation with enable_fp_fusion=False) adds rounding error that pushes the total error above 1e-6 for some in-range FP16 inputs even independent of coefficient truncation.
